chunks: Asim ibn Humayd narrated from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja‘far عليه السلام, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام ruled concerning a mukatab who had a free woman as his wife, and she made a bequest for him at the time of her death. He said: 'The heirs are not to allow her bequest for him, for he is a mukatab who has not been freed.'

Then he عليه السلام ruled that he would inherit in proportion to the amount of him that had been freed, and that the bequest would be valid for him in proportion to the amount of him that had been freed.
And he عليه السلام ruled regarding a mukatab for whom a bequest had been made, and he had paid half of what was due from him, that half of the bequest was valid for him.
And he ruled regarding a mukatab who had paid a quarter of what was due from him, and a bequest had been made for him, that a quarter of the bequest was valid for him.

And he عليه السلام said concerning a man who made a bequest for his female mukatabah, and she had paid one-sixth of what was due from her, that he validated it for her in proportion to the amount of her that had been freed.

key_terms.أُعْتِقَ: was freed; denotes the proportion of manumission already completed
key_terms.الْمِيرَاثِ: inheritance due to legal heirs after a person's death
key_terms.رُبُعَ: quarter; used here for proportional legal entitlement
key_terms.سُدُسَ: one-sixth; used here for proportional legal entitlement
key_terms.مُكَاتَبٍ: a slave under a manumission contract, whose legal status is partially tied to payments made
key_terms.نِصْفَ: half; used here for proportional legal entitlement
key_terms.وَصِيَّةٍ: a bequest or testamentary gift made to take effect after death
key_terms.يَرِثُ: inherits; receives a legally recognized share of inheritance

ai.seo_question: How are inheritance and bequests calculated for a mukatab in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith records legal rulings from Amir al-Mu'minin عليه السلام concerning the inheritance and bequests of a mukatab, a slave under a contractual manumission arrangement. The ruling establishes that such a person receives inheritance and testamentary benefit only in proportion to the amount of freedom already attained through payment.
